hook: The James Webb Space Telescope just found an object only 3 times the mass of Jupiter.

sections.voiceover: The James Webb Space Telescope just found an object only 3 times the mass of Jupiter.
sections.visual_cue: Close-up of the James Webb Space Telescope in space.

sections.voiceover: Located 1,000 light-years away in the Perseus constellation, the IC 348 star cluster is a nursery for young stars. How can a free-floating object be this small?
sections.visual_cue: Wide view of the IC 348 cluster with stars highlighted.

sections.voiceover: Yet NIRSpec spectrograph data showed this IC 348 target isn't a normal star.
sections.visual_cue: Animation showing a cooling, dimming brown dwarf.

sections.voiceover: Researchers confirmed the object has a mass between 3 and 4 Jupiter masses. NIRSpec spectrograph analysis confirmed it's the lowest-mass brown dwarf ever detected with spectroscopy.
sections.visual_cue: Comparison graphic showing the brown dwarf next to Jupiter.

sections.voiceover: Astronomers use the James Webb Space Telescope's NIRSpec spectrograph to scan IC 348.
sections.visual_cue: Deep field view of stars slowly fading to black.
